questions.solution:
I-1 (binary semaphore = 1): mutual exclusion, so every update is applied: [latex]V_1=10+5-3=12[/latex].

I-2 (counting semaphore = 2): two threads can be inside together and updates can be lost. To get the minimum:
- a decr thread reads X = 10 and is preempted;
- all 5 incr threads run one after another (using the second slot): X = 15;
- the first decr writes 10 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 9, wiping out all 5 increments;
- the other 2 decr run normally: X = 7.

So [latex]V_2=7[/latex].

Answer: 12, 7

questions.text:
Which one or more of the following CPU scheduling algorithms can potentially
cause starvation?
questions.solution:
Check whether a process can wait forever:
- FIFO: every process eventually reaches the front [latex]\text{---}[/latex] no starvation.
- Round Robin: each process gets a time slice every round [latex]\text{---}[/latex] no starvation.
- Priority scheduling: a low-priority process may wait forever if high-priority processes keep arriving.
- SJF: a long job may wait forever if short jobs keep arriving.

Answer: Priority Scheduling, Shortest Job First

questions.text:
Which one or more of the following options guarantee that a computer system will
transition from user mode to kernel mode?
questions.solution:
Check which events always enter the kernel:
- Function call: runs entirely in user mode [latex]\text{---}[/latex] no switch.
- malloc: a library function; it usually takes memory from the existing heap and makes a system call only sometimes [latex]\text{---}[/latex] not guaranteed.
- Page fault: an exception handled by the OS [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] always kernel mode.
- System call: a trap into the kernel [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] always kernel mode.

Answer: Page Fault, System Call

questions.text:
Which one or more of the following need to be saved on a context switch from one
thread (T1) of a process to another thread (T2) of the same process?
questions.solution:
Threads of the same process share the address space, so the page table base register does not change and need not be saved.

Each thread has its own execution context: stack pointer, program counter and general purpose registers [latex]\text{---}[/latex] these must be saved.

Answer: Stack pointer, Program counter, General purpose registers

questions.text:
Consider a demand paging system with four page frames (initially empty) and LRU page replacement policy. For the following page reference string

7, 2, 7, 3, 2, 5, 3, 4, 6, 7, 7,1, 5, 6,1

the page fault rate, defined as the ratio of number of page faults to the number of memory accesses (rounded off to one decimal place) is
questions.solution:
LRU with 4 frames (F = fault):
7 F, 2 F, 7 hit, 3 F, 2 hit, 5 F [7, 2, 3, 5], 3 hit,
4 F (evict 7), 6 F (evict 2), 7 F (evict 5), 7 hit, 1 F (evict 3), 5 F (evict 4), 6 hit, 1 hit.

Faults = 9 out of 15 references. Rate [latex]=\frac{9}{15}=0.6[/latex]

Answer: 0.6
